paper.title_en: Deep learning for extensive air showers reconstruction: An interpretable multi-task CNN-Transformer model for the CONDOR observatory
paper.abstract_en: The reconstruction of extensive air showers (EAS) is a critical task, particularly in cosmic ray observatories. In this work, we present a multi-task deep learning framework for reconstructing EAS at the CONDOR Observatory, a proposed high-altitude gamma-ray experiment in northern Chile. Our model, based on a hybrid CNN–Transformer architecture, simultaneously performs zenith angle reconstruction, gamma–hadron showers discrimination, and primary energy estimation, using variable-length sequences of discretized detector hits in space and time. Trained on CORSIKA-simulated data, the model achieves an F1-score of <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1482"><mo>∼</mo></math>97.2% for gamma–hadron discrimination, a mean angular error of around 0.5 degrees, and <math altimg="si4.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1487"><mrow><mn>103.3</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="1em"/><mi mathvariant="normal">GeV</mi></mrow></math> mean absolute error for energy estimation across the 300–800 GeV range. In addition, we use explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) techniques, such as permutation feature importance (PFI) and attention pattern analysis, to enhance interpretability. The results show that different channels contribute unequally to each task, with temporal information being critical for angle reconstruction and spatial features dominating classification. These findings confirm that the artificial neural network learns physically meaningful representations of shower evolution, and that explainability tools can support model validation and insight extraction. The proposed approach offers a scalable and interpretable solution for event reconstruction in next-generation astroparticle observatories.
